name: io.github.MsingathiM/swapeazi
title: SwapEazi
description: Payment intelligence for agents sending money abroad or paying suppliers.

tools.name: discover_payment
tools.description: Use when a user wants to send money abroad or pay a supplier, for example 'pay GBP 1,000 to Botswana' or 'send EUR 1,000 to Botswana'. Ask for the recipient currency if it is not specified; do not assume it from the country. Provide amount, source_currency and target_currency, and beneficiary.country when known. Returns available payment evidence, costs, timing, requirements and unknowns for the currency pair; coverage varies and some facts may be unavailable. A reference rate or indicative figure is not a firm quote. The compact response points to a signed Options Map; detail: "full" returns the full report. An optional needed_by adds timing and FX scenarios, not a forecast or recommendation. The customer decides and their provider executes the payment.

amount.description: The amount, greater than zero.

source_currency.description: ISO 4217 code the payment leaves in, e.g. 'EUR'.

target_currency.description: ISO 4217 code the payment must land in, e.g. 'ZAR'.

direction.description: pay (default): amount is what leaves. receive: amount is what must land.

amount_in.description: Which currency amount is stated in. Overrides direction's default, e.g. paying a fixed destination amount while funding from the source currency.

needed_by.description: Optional ISO date the money must land by. Adds timing_scenarios, fx_exposure and hedge_scenarios to the report, and each option's settlement.release_by: the latest release that lands by this date at the rail's later and earlier typical settle_days (on bank rails, the provider's cut-off on a banking day; the cut-off is not on record).

release_at.description: Optional ISO date-time the payment will be released; default now. Each option's settlement.release_window states whether its rail moves at that moment (bank rails on banking days only, stablecoin rails around the clock), when it starts moving, the landing dates that follow, any sourced time-based markup, and what is not on record (cut-offs, bank holidays).

entity_type.description: corporate, sme, fintech, crypto_native or individual.

jurisdiction.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the payer.

payer.description: Optional. Who is paying: { entity_type, jurisdiction }.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country where the supplier is paid, e.g. 'CN'.

beneficiary.description: Optional. Where the supplier is paid: { country }. Its country rules on record (and the payer's, from payer.jurisdiction) are returned as country_rules.

rails_allowed.description: Default: all. Only bank and stablecoin filter directly today; psp/dex leave every non-excluded rail in.

current_quote.description: Optional: a quote already held, measured as given against the reference.

provider.description: Who gave the quote, e.g. a bank or provider name.

quoted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the quote was given, e.g. '2026-11-04T09:30:00Z'.

max_settlement_hours.description: Maximum hours from release to landing; slower options are marked outside.

exclude_providers.description: Provider ids or names to leave out.

require_licensed_in.description: Not yet filterable; listed in what_we_dont_know when given.

constraints.description: Optional. The payer's own limits: { max_settlement_hours, exclude_providers, require_licensed_in }.

client.description: Optional. Who is asking: { type: agent | human, agent_id }.

detail.description: compact (default): a short summary that points at the signed full document, sized for a tool result. full: the whole document, which can exceed 100 KB.

tools.name: run_payments
tools.description: Prepares a batch of cross-border payments for approval: validates each payee, prices each route and drafts each instruction for the business's own bank, provider or wallet. Send the payables (payables: a JSON list; file: a payout CSV or pain.001; or xero: a Xero bills reply) with source_currency. Each payment is verified (changed bank details against previous, duplicates, missing fields), assessed (route assessment_id with Rate Receipts: who published each figure, when it was read, its evidence type) and given an instruction for the business's own bank, provider or wallet (a CSV row, or an unsigned stablecoin transaction). Each is prepared, needs_attention (with the reason) or no_evidence. Returns run_id. An agent prepares; a named person approves. Never sends or moves money. A router key runs real payables; without one, sample: true returns the synthetic sample run. Same as POST /api/v1/payment-runs.

sample.description: true: the built-in sample run (synthetic, labelled), no key needed.

source_currency.description: The currency the business pays from, e.g. ZAR.

payables.description: [{ reference, payee: { name, iban?, bic?, account_number?, routing_number?, branch_code?, country? }, amount, currency, due_date?, rail?: bank | provider | stablecoin, via?, wallet? }]

file.description: Instead of payables: a payout CSV or pain.001 text.

previous.description: The previous run's payables, for changed bank details and amount jumps. Not kept.

sort.description: Your chosen order for the routes: landed cost against the official rate, stated days to land, or the measured 7-day answer rate. It is your order, stated as yours. Without it, routes come in the order the sources answered; get_corridor_capacity ranks routes by evidence of what landed.

include_types.description: Keep only routes of these rail types. Each route left out is listed with the reason.

exclude_types.description: Leave out routes of these rail types. Each route left out is listed with the reason.

min_answer_rate.description: Percent, 0 to 100: leave out routes whose measured 7-day answer rate is lower, or not measured (not enough reads). Each is listed with the reason.

access_key.description: A router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.

tools.name: approve_payment_run
tools.description: Gets prepared payments approved by a named person and returns each one's release instruction. Records the approval of that person (approver: { name, role }) for the run's prepared payments (payments: "all_prepared") or listed payment_ids (held ones need acknowledge: true), and creates one release record per approved payment. Each approved payment returns release_in_own_bank: beneficiary, amount, currency, reference, which of the business's own accounts to pay from and the cut-off, for the business to release itself in its own bank or rail portal; then record what landed with reconcile_payment. An agent cannot approve on its own: this tool records an approval only when the run's policy sets agent_may_record_approval and names the person who approved; otherwise it returns how the person approves (POST /api/v1/payment-runs/{id}/approve). Never sends or moves money.

approver.description: { name, role, id? }: the person who approved. Required.

acknowledge.description: true to approve listed payments that need attention or have no evidence, once the person has assessed them.

access_key.description: A router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.

tools.name: payment_run_status
tools.description: Tracks each payment in a run from prepared through approval and release to what landed. Reads the run by run_id: each payment's status (prepared, needs_attention with reasons, no_evidence), its assessment and Rate Receipts, approval, release record and what landed. export: true returns the audit export, where any payment without an assessment, approval or release record shows "no evidence". pr_sample needs no key; a real run needs the router key that made it.

export.description: true: the audit export (JSON) instead of the run.

access_key.description: A router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.

tools.name: recommend_payment_route
tools.description: Prepares one payment: the routes that can carry it, with cost, speed, licence and freshness. Hard facts first (complete cost, not stale, settles by the due date, licence active, not excluded by route health). SwapEazi does not pick a route. A person chooses. Not a firm quote: confirm with the provider before approval. One analysis (POST /api/v1/payment-analyses), the same service for every payment-intelligence tool. Every figure labelled LIVE, INDICATIVE, HISTORICAL or ESTIMATED. Free: shares the route-assessment allowance.

invoice_text.description: Paste the invoice or a sentence (e.g. 'Invoice INV-2207, Lusaka Copper Supplies Ltd, Zambia. Amount due: EUR 80,000. Due 2026-11-20'). Or the fields below.

amount.description: Amount, in currency (default the source currency).

currency.description: The currency of amount: the source currency, or the destination one (then it is what the supplier receives).

source_currency.description: ISO code you pay from, e.g. EUR or ZAR.

destination_currency.description: ISO code the supplier is paid in, e.g. ZMW. Or destination_country.

destination_country.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 or name, e.g. ZM or Mozambique.

beneficiary_amount.description: What the supplier must receive, in the destination currency (instead of amount).

due_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD: a route that cannot settle by then is not eligible.

priority.description: Sets the default scoring weights. Default balanced.

weights.description: Your own scoring weights: { total_cost, speed, reliability, liquidity, compliance }, non-negative, normalised to 1.

existing_provider.description: Your current provider: { provider, kind: quote | entered_rate | past_payment, rate (destination per source unit) or landed_amount, fees: { transaction, intermediary, payout } in the source currency, fees_deducted_destination, quoted_at, valid_until }.

supplier.description: Optional. The supplier's name as on the invoice, e.g. 'Lusaka Copper Supplies Ltd'; echoed in the analysis.

reference.description: Optional. Your invoice or payment reference, e.g. 'INV-2207'; echoed in the analysis.

analysis_id.description: Read a kept analysis (pa_...) instead of making a new one.

access_key.description: A router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header: names the routes and is not counted.

tools.name: assess_route
tools.description: Prices a cross-border payment before the business commits to it: every known route for the pair, assessed on SwapEazi's independent data. Returns deterministic JSON: the routes known for the pair, each cost and FX figure with its source, read time, freshness (fresh, aging, stale, unknown) and evidence type (observed, executable, indicative, published; the official rate as reference), settlement facts, the requirements on record with sources, what changed since the last assessment of the corridor, data-quality flags (stale, contradictory, missing, indicative only), unknowns, and the evidence behind each finding, under an assessment_id whose record is kept and retrievable (GET /api/v1/route-assessments/{id}; a content hash, not a signature). Never recommends a route, never executes, never claims a figure is executable unless a provider's firm quote is on record. Free; same as GET /api/v1/route-assessments.

from.description: Source currency, ISO code, e.g. EUR.

to.description: Destination currency, ISO code, e.g. ZMW.

corridor.description: Instead of from and to: e.g. EUR-ZMW.

amount.description: Amount leaving, in the source currency. Optional: without it the corridor is assessed at about USD 10,000, labelled.

as_of.description: Assessment time, ISO 8601, within 15 minutes of now (default now). A past assessment is retrieved by assessment_id, never recomputed.

assessment_id.description: Retrieve a kept assessment record instead of making a new one.

sort.description: Your chosen order for the routes: landed cost against the official rate, stated days to land, or the measured 7-day answer rate. It is your order, stated as yours. Without it, routes come in the order the sources answered; get_corridor_capacity ranks routes by evidence of what landed.

include_types.description: Keep only routes of these rail types. Each route left out is listed with the reason.

exclude_types.description: Leave out routes of these rail types. Each route left out is listed with the reason.

min_answer_rate.description: Percent, 0 to 100: leave out routes whose measured 7-day answer rate is lower, or not measured (not enough reads). Each is listed with the reason.

payer_country.description: Two-letter country the money leaves from. Needed when from and to are the same currency (e.g. USD from LR to a USD account in CN): the payment is then assessed as a cross-border transfer, banks' charges and rules, no conversion.

beneficiary_country.description: Two-letter country of the beneficiary's account; with payer_country for a same-currency payment.

charge_option.description: Who pays the banks' charges on a wire: OUR (payer pays all), SHA (shared), BEN (beneficiary).

tools.name: liquidity_map
tools.description: Shows where a payment of this size can be filled, and at what cost. For a currency pair (e.g. ZAR-USD, NGN-USD, KES-USD, USD-MWK) and a ticket size: each venue type (exchange order books, stablecoin pools, P2P adverts, ramps and off-ramps, OTC desks, banks) with whether the evidence read shows depth at that size, the measured slippage and landing cost at that size with a Rate Receipt, the largest size the evidence supports, or Being measured with the reason. With prefunding (amount held, days held), idle fiat prefunding and stablecoin reserves on the same evidence: cost to enter and exit at that size, the peg and exit depth from the stablecoin profiles, and the past official-rate move over the same days. Figures, not advice. Unknowns listed. SwapEazi never holds, creates or moves liquidity. Free callers see Route A, Route B; a router key shows venue names. Same as GET/POST /api/v1/liquidity.

pair.description: e.g. ZAR-USD or USD-MWK. Or from and to.

from.description: ISO 4217 code of the source currency (what leaves), e.g. 'ZAR'.

to.description: ISO 4217 code of the destination currency (what lands), e.g. 'USD'.

amount.description: Ticket size, in the from currency unless amount_currency says otherwise.

amount_currency.description: The from or the to currency. Default from.

prefunding.description: { amount, currency?, corridor?, days_held }: an amount held to prefund the corridor, and for how many days (1 to 365).

access_key.description: A router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.

tools.name: onchain_liquidity
tools.description: Finds where a stablecoin payment of this size can be filled on-chain, and at what cost: for USDC and USDT (and ZARP, cNGN as to_asset), executable depth and cost at the amount on Ethereum, Tron, Solana, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum and Polygon, from keyless DEX aggregator quotes (KyberSwap, ParaSwap, Jupiter): price impact against a USD 100 quote, cost against par with gas and stated fees, and each network's published time to finality. Bridge cost and time between chains from Across, Circle CCTP and LI.FI. Each chain's network fee model (EIP-1559 base fee plus tip, BNB gas price, Solana's fixed fee plus priority fee, Tron energy; HyperEVM labelled unconfirmed) with the fee for one transfer in USD and in bps of the ticket, and its 24-hour range from stored reads. The hourly reads at USD 10k, 100k, 1m and 5m for the pair, each with its age. With destination (two-letter country), the documented facts on whether suppliers there take stablecoins directly (not established where we hold no source) and the off-ramp venues SwapEazi reads in its currency. Every figure has its source, time and a Rate Receipt; each failure keeps its reason. Figures, not advice. The SwapEazi check never touches the money and never asks for a wallet signature. Same as GET/POST /api/v1/onchain-liquidity. Free within the daily allowance.

amount.description: The ticket in US dollars (dollar stablecoins at par).

to_asset.description: USDC, USDT, ZARP or cNGN (ZAR and NGN map to ZARP and cNGN). Default: the other dollar coin.

chains.description: Any of ethereum, tron, solana, base, bsc, arbitrum, polygon. Default all.

destination.description: Optional supplier country, two letters (e.g. HK, CN, AE, NG, ZA, KE).

access_key.description: A router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header: shows exchange and P2P venue names in the destination block.

tools.name: record_landed
tools.description: Closes a payment once the money arrived, on its remembered intent: what left (source currency) and what arrived (destination currency), and/or attach a stablecoin leg by chain and transaction hash, verified from the chain. SwapEazi measures it against the independent reference and against what was routed, and every later route on the pair carries it as a measured payment. On a recurring intent it closes the current cycle only and the series moves to its next due date. Amounts only, never names or account numbers.

intent_id.description: The remembered intent to close (remembered.intent_id from route_intent).

sent.description: Amount that left, in the source currency.

landed.description: Amount that arrived, in the destination currency, after every deduction.

provider.description: Defaults to the route selected on the last day.

chain.description: For a stablecoin leg: base, ethereum, arbitrum, optimism, polygon or celo.

tx.description: For a stablecoin leg: the transaction hash; read and priced from the chain and added to the payment record.

tools.name: reconcile_payment
tools.description: Matches each released payment in a run with what landed: amount sent, amount landed, settlement time, proof reference, the official rate with a Rate Receipt, realised all-in cost in percent and in the sent currency, and position inside, above or below the assessment range. The same proof reference is rejected the second time. dry_run: true validates and writes nothing. A payment with no assessment is flagged no_evidence. A router key is required except for pr_sample. Never sends money.

payments.description: [{ payment_id, sent_amount, landed_amount, settled_at?, proof_ref, source? }]. proof_ref is an MT103 reference, a transaction hash or a provider reference.

access_key.description: A router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.

tools.name: record_release
tools.description: Records the release of a material payment against the organisation's release policy, at the moment it is released: the map_id and measure_id on file, who released it, and any exception with its reason and approver. When an agent releases under a policy with agent_autonomy tiers, the record states the tier its amount falls in and the agent_approval on record for it. Returns a Release Evidence Record, appended to the organisation's hash chain and signed. It records; it never blocks, executes or moves money. A release with no map is still recorded, flagged as a policy miss. Needs the organisation's key.

policy_id.description: The organisation's release policy the payment is released under, e.g. 'pol_...'.

payment_ref.description: Your internal payment reference, never an account number.

uetr.description: The payment's SWIFT UETR (UUID v4), optional: ties the record to the payment itself.

value.description: Amount released, in amount.currency, greater than zero.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the released amount, e.g. 'EUR'.

amount.description: The released amount: { value, currency }.

map_id.description: The Options Map (map_id) on file for this payment, if one was made.

measure_id.description: The Measure (msr_...) on file for this payment, if one was made.

intent_hash.description: The intent_hash from compile_intent, so the record proves the map matches this payment.

id.description: Your own id for the releaser, e.g. an employee id or agent id; never a password or key.

released_by.description: Who released the payment: { type: human | system | agent, id }.

reason.description: Why the payment was released outside the policy, in plain words.

id.description: Your own id for the approver.

approved_by.description: The person who approved the exception: { id, role }.

exception.description: Only when the release falls outside the policy: { reason, approved_by: { id, role } }.

agent_approval.description: Agent releases only: { id, role } of the person who signed off a release above the policy's agent_autonomy.release_up_to. The role is the policy's agent_autonomy.approver_role.

id.description: Your own id for the person who signed off.

tools.name: release_status
tools.description: Tracks a released payment's evidence: reads its Release Evidence Record by rer_id: the policy result at release and the match status as of now (pending, done, overdue or not required). With no rer_id, verifies the organisation's chain of records and returns ok or the first record where it breaks. Read-only. Needs the organisation's key.

rer_id.description: Optional. The Release Evidence Record (rer_...) to read. Omit to verify the organisation's whole chain.

tools.name: check_fx_charges
tools.description: Every foreign-currency cost on a bank or card statement found, proven and booked. Give files (statement CSV, or PDF/screenshot; supplier invoices) or transactions[] and invoices[]. Each charge is matched to its invoice, rated at the ECB mid of the transaction date (last business day on weekends and holidays, date and source named), split into hidden markup in the rate, disclosed fee and VAT, booked as balanced journals in the functional currency (settings: functional_currency, chart_of_accounts, accounting_policy), with exceptions flagged (verification charges, failed attempts, refunds netted, no conversion, vendor reference rates never trusted, cashback, duplicates blocked). Returns a signed, re-runnable pack: same input, same pack_id, hashes and signature. Read-only: SwapEazi never touches the money. Free up to 20 transactions a month; unlimited with a key.

files.description: [{ name, data (CSV text or base64 PDF/image), kind?: statement|invoice, currency? (account currency when the CSV has none), account? }]

transactions.description: [{ date, description, amount (negative = money out), currency, foreign_amount?, foreign_currency?, bank_rate?, fee?, vat?, cashback?, processing_date?, status?, chain?, tx_hash? }]

invoices.description: [{ vendor, number?, date, amount, currency, vat?, reference_currency?, reference_amount?, reference_rate? }]

settings.description: { functional_currency?, chart_of_accounts?, accounting_policy?: { fx_cost: separate_account|in_expense, expense_rate_date: invoice|charge }, period_end?, match_window_days? }

consent.description: Add the result anonymously to the public markup index

provider.description: Your bank or card, from the public index list (fnb, absa, ing, revolut, ...); anything else is stored as other. Used only with consent.

card_type.description: Card type, for the anonymous index. Used only with consent.

tools.name: books_record
tools.description: A books-ready, standards-referenced record of one managed payment for the payer's own books: the invoice in the functional currency at approval and at settlement at dated official rates (ECB for EUR, SARB for ZAR, named with date), fees split out, the realised FX difference between approval and settlement, the conversion cost against the official rate, the landed amount, stablecoin legs each valued at its own time with the measured premium (classification left to the company's accountant), and the Rate Receipt and release record ids. Give run_id (+ payment_id) for a Payment Run (pr_sample works without a key), or the figures (business, payment, legs). format: json (record + suggested journal lines, accounts left to the company), csv or journal. closing: { date, currencies } adds the period-end closing rate for open balances. SwapEazi posts nothing to any ledger and decides no accounting policy.

payment_id.description: One payment of the run; all payments when left out.

business.description: { name?, country (ISO 2), functional_currency? (defaults from country), framework?: IFRS | US_GAAP | LOCAL_GAAP }

payment.description: { invoice?: {amount, currency}, sent: {amount, currency}, landed?: {amount, currency}, approved_at, settled_at?, fees?: [{label, amount, currency, paid_by?: payer|beneficiary}], reference?, payee? }

legs.description: Stablecoin legs: [{ at, kind: conversion|transfer|payout, from: {amount, currency}, to: {amount, currency}, venue?, ref? }]

format.description: json (default): the record with suggested journal lines; csv; or journal lines only.

closing.description: { date: YYYY-MM-DD, currencies: ["USD", "USDC"], functional? }: period-end closing rates with source.

access_key.description: The router key that made the run (not needed for pr_sample or given figures).

tools.name: swapeazi_coverage
tools.description: Every currency a payment can be measured in today, and the number of directional corridors between them. Call before swapeazi_landed_cost to know whether a pair is covered. Free, no key.

tools.name: swapeazi_corridor_registry
tools.description: Documented status of cross-border corridors per provider: which pairs a provider says it serves, published fees, and when each record was last verified. Public tier only. Free, no key.

from.description: Optional ISO 4217 source currency, e.g. 'ZAR'.

to.description: Optional ISO 4217 destination currency, e.g. 'ZMW'.

tools.name: swapeazi_guardrail_check
tools.description: Before money moves: every eligible route for a payment scored against your own limits (maximum LDI, maximum settlement time, regulated provider required), your quote measured if you pass one, beside what banks advertise, the official business-payment average and the G20 lines. Evidence against your policy, never a recommendation. Returns a signed record: keep it with the payment and pass it to swapeazi_guardrail_reconcile once it settles. Paid: configure this server with an Authorization Bearer key (https://swapeazi.io/pricing).

client_id.description: Optional. Your own reference, echoed back.

source_amount.description: Amount to send, in the origin currency.

origin_jurisdiction.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the sender.

destination_jurisdiction.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the beneficiary.

max_acceptable_ldi_bps.description: Optional. Your cost cap in basis points.

quote.description: Optional. A quote you already hold, to be measured as given.

provider.description: Who gave the quote, e.g. a bank or provider name; for the record, not used to price.

landed_amount.description: Amount the quote says will land, in the destination currency.

allowed_providers.description: Optional. Restrict routes to your own already-connected panel, by provider label or id. For embedding this assessment as a mandatory step inside your own already-licensed release pipeline. asking which of YOUR connected providers should carry this, not who exists in the market, the way an execution-management system asks which of its own connected brokers should fill an order. A provider outside the panel is ruled out before scoring, never silently dropped: it appears in ruled_out with reason not_in_callers_connected_panel. Omit for no restriction.

tools.name: swapeazi_guardrail_reconcile
tools.description: After money moves: the signed record from swapeazi_guardrail_check plus what landed (figures, or the bank's MT103 or pacs.008 text) returns a signed matching record. Was the quote honoured, did the payment stay inside policy, how far the market moved between approval and value date, and which part of the cost the banks in the chain took. Only amounts, dates, rates and charges are read from a message, never the parties. Paid, included in the assessment it closes.

settlement.description: What landed, when no bank message is supplied.

landed_amount.description: Amount that arrived, in the destination currency.

source_amount.description: Optional. Amount that left, including any fee billed on top.

message.description: Optional. The bank's MT103 text or pacs.008 XML for this payment.

tools.name: swapeazi_verify_record
tools.description: Verify that a decision or matching record was issued by SwapEazi and has not been altered, and read what it says. Free and keyless, so an auditor, board or counterparty can verify a payer's records without an account.

attestation.description: The attestation string from a decision or matching record.

tools.name: verify_release_record
tools.description: Verify a SwapEazi Release Record v1, the evidence of a managed payment (or a chain of them), with no key: schema (https://swapeazi.io/schemas/release-record-v1.json), hash, chain link and Ed25519 signature against the published key. Returns valid or invalid with each test named and the first record that breaks. Nothing sent is stored. The same verification runs offline from the spec at https://swapeazi.io/standard.

record.description: One release record, as returned by record_release, release_status or GET /api/v1/releases/{id}.

chain.description: Optional. The records around it, in any order; links are verified in seq order.

tools.name: swapeazi_beneficiary_check
tools.description: Structural check on a payment destination: an IBAN's own checksum (ISO 7064 MOD 97-10), a US ABA routing number's own checksum, a BIC's format (ISO 9362), an EVM address's EIP-55 checksum, a South African universal branch code recognised against known major banks, or a SADC mobile-money number (South Africa, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Zambia) assessed for the right country code and length. Catches a mistyped or mis-keyed identifier, the single most common cause of a misdirected payment. A payment platform is several rails at once (SEPA, Fedwire/ACH, stablecoin); this assessments whichever identifiers you supply. UK sort codes and most domestic account numbers carry no public checksum and are not covered. This is NOT confirmation of payee or verification of payee: it does not confirm the name on the account, only that the identifier is internally consistent (or, for a branch code or phone number, plausible). Paid: configure this server with an Authorization Bearer key (https://swapeazi.io/pricing).

usRoutingNumber.description: A US ABA routing number, 9 digits.

saBranchCode.description: A South African universal branch code, 6 digits.

mxClabe.description: A Mexican CLABE (SPEI account), 18 digits; its verification digit is verified.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the mobile-money number: ZA, ZW, MW or ZM.

address.description: An EVM address, '0x' followed by 40 hex characters.

tools.name: payout_preflight
tools.description: Pre-release check on a whole payout file before it goes to the company's own bank or PSP. Send the file's text: an ISO 20022 pain.001 credit-transfer file (versions .03 to .12) or a CSV with a header row (comma or semicolon, Dutch or English column names). Every row comes back ok, needs_person or blocked, with the reasons: missing name or account, failed IBAN checksum, a BIC from a different country than the IBAN, SA branch code, SADC mobile money, too many decimals, a euro payment outside SEPA, an execution date in the past or on a weekend, possible duplicates, and rows above the company's own review limit. With a signing key set, it also returns a signed record of the check (file hash and each row's state, no names or accounts). SwapEazi never sends, holds or routes the money: the company releases the file itself. Paid: configure this server with an Authorization Bearer key (https://swapeazi.io/pricing).

file.description: The payout file's text: pain.001 XML or a CSV with a header row.

today.description: Release date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today (UTC).

review_above.description: Rows above this amount need a person, whatever else they pass. The company's own limit.

tools.name: map_options
tools.description: The signed Options Map for a PaymentIntent: every rail and provider the graph holds for the pair and size, each with its access facts, documented capacity, settlement window, economics basis (observed, band or unpublished) and evidence class, and whether it sits inside, outside or unknown against the principal's constraints. Each candidate also carries route_family (bank_correspondent or stablecoin_casp), regulatory_risk (stable, watch, restricted or blocked, tied to a tracked rule) and onboarding_status (ready, onboardable, ineligible or unknown, with onboarding_gap naming what's missing) so an agent can filter out ineligible or blocked routes before quoting. route_families lists every family even one with zero candidates, reason no_eligible_provider, rather than hiding it. Sorted by coverage tier, rail class and name, never by a rank. payout_rules lists the rules that reach the payout per route (applies or depends, each with its document; document_not_read when found by search). A guide, not advice. Pass an intent (any form compile_intent takes, including payer) or an intent_id. Free within the daily allowance; a key lifts it. Returns a compact view by default (one short object per candidate, every unknown in full) that points at the signed full map; pass detail: "full" for the whole signed document, or map_id to read back a map made earlier.

tools.name: check_constraints

Each row comes back inside, outside or unknown, and carries the map's own route_family, regulatory_risk and onboarding_status/onboarding_gap for that candidate, so an agent can drop ineligible or blocked rows without a second call. Nothing is executed or issued. Free.

tools.name: route_intent
tools.description: Route one cross-border payment, given as fields or as one sentence ("USD 25,000 to a supplier in Lagos by 30 November"). From a sentence the guide reads what matters without being told: urgency or the due date sets the deadline and puts speed first, words such as cheapest put cost first, regulated or licensed keeps only providers with a licence on record, and paying drivers, staff or a supplier is noted; intent.understood says what was read, and explicit policy fields override it. Returns every route that can carry it, ordered by the payer's own policy, the route the policy selects on the strongest evidence (payments measured when they landed, then published prices; estimates only if the policy allows), the saving against the payer's own quote, and where to pay. With a due date it also routes across time: pay now, lock a forward while holding tokenised T-bills, convert and park, or hold unhedged, as what each needs today. With remember: true SwapEazi keeps the intent, reprices it daily until due and returns its intent_id. A sentence about idle money ("park $5m USDC, back within 24 hours, non-US, qualified, we have Ondo") returns treasury parking instead: tokenised T-bill funds that fit the amount, eligibility, chain and redemption need, by net yield, with what the accounts already held can do and what a new account is worth. The free verification returns the verdict with names masked; a router key (Bearer rk_...) unlocks them. SwapEazi executes nothing and takes no fee from any provider. Returns a compact view by default (each route with its release window cut to the summary and landing dates); pass detail: "full" for everything.

from.description: ISO 4217 code of the source currency (what leaves), e.g. 'ZAR'.

to.description: ISO 4217 code of the destination currency (what lands), e.g. 'USD'.

Signed. Facts only; SwapEazi moves no money.

tools.name: prepare_payment
tools.description: Prepare an unsigned USDC or USDT transaction for the paying wallet you control, on Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon or BNB Chain, or USDT (TRC-20) on Tron (chain_id 728126428, T... addresses; TronLink signs it). SwapEazi screens the recipient's address and verifies the organisation's spend profile first: the cap per payment, the daily and monthly budget, approved recipients and chains, and the approval line. A person approves every payment an agent prepares: within the rules it returns an approval_id, the approver decides at /approvals, and once approved payment_controls with that approval_id returns the transaction (a plain transfer, or a swap or bridge with no SwapEazi fee) for your wallet to sign; outside the rules it explains why. Pass the map_id and candidate_id of the stablecoin option you took from discover_payment or map_options, so the approver sees what the guide showed for it and the records name the map; the guide never picks it. SwapEazi never signs, holds keys or moves funds. With private: true, the payment runs through NEAR Intents' confidential mode under the same rules; that is also the way between Tron and an EVM chain. With profile_id, needs the organisation's key.

With approval_id, reads that one approval. Read-only. Needs the organisation's key.

Use it before acting on a payment, to see what is current, what has expired and what must happen next. Read-only: it changes nothing and moves no money. Cases opened with an organisation's key need that key.

Each decision is signed and chained to the agent's signed record. Do not release a payout while it is awaiting approval, rejected or expired. Read-only. Each event carries its source link and an evidence label: 'official source' (a regulator or central bank published it), 'announced, unverified' (a company or the press reported it), or 'headline only, not read'. tools.name: rail_handoff
tools.description: Keyed. With intent_id: after a person has approved, the approved instruction for your rail, with a Rate Receipt of the rate against the official rate and the negotiated deal; where no live connection is configured the adapter is marked stub. The default is that the business releases the payment itself in its own bank or rail portal (release_in_own_bank on the approved payment); SwapEazi never sends it. Sandbox only: with run_id, payment_id and connection_id, sends ONE Payment Run payment a named person approved through the business's OWN connected rail account (Yellow Card sandbox; production stays off unless the deployment sets YELLOWCARD_ENV=production), with the rail's own idempotency key, and returns the submission with a Rate Receipt and the release record. Refused, with the reason, without a recorded approval, when the payment changed since approval, above the connection's cap, or for an account other than the one approved. With run_id and payment_id only: reads that payment's status from the rail. SwapEazi holds no funds and has no account in the flow.

The credentials are proven with a read (no payment is sent), encrypted at rest and never returned: answers show the key's last four characters and the created date. tools.name: get_corridor_capacity
tools.description: Which banks, fintechs, stablecoin platforms and crypto P2P routes can carry one payment, e.g. 'Pay EUR 100k to Botswana', each measured the same way: corridor served (or one leg only), can carry it (yes / no / not established, against a published per-payment limit or measured P2P depth, with the source), licence in the sending and receiving country with the register, cost against the official rate (Rate Receipt where priced; otherwise 'listed, not priced', never estimated), stated speed, on/off-ramp and stablecoin path, and the forms of money each takes (bank deposit, tokenised deposit, USDC, USDT, EURC, PYUSD...) with the chains where published and whether it cashes out in the destination currency. Public sources only, every fact with its source URL and date; routes ranked by evidence of what landed (landing receipts, then verified business submissions, then public reports, each labelled), not enough evidence yet where it is thin, with landing time and delay risk next to cost; a listing never changes rank. Paid per call: x402 (USDC on Base, price in the 402 body, USD 0.25) via params._meta["x402/payment"], or a paid router key as Bearer. The free top line is GET https://swapeazi.io/api/v1/capacity. Who does what: the agent may compile the intent, gather the facts, propose the route that fits the user's own weights (recommend_payment_route) and prepare the instruction with a link to the provider's own sign-in. A person approves, releases, shares account details and authorises any spend above the mandate; the user signs in to the provider with their own credentials. SwapEazi never touches the money: it never connects a wallet and never asks for a signature.

tools.name: get_payment_guide

Leads with paying and getting paid: the banks, fintechs, stablecoin platforms and crypto routes on record that can carry the payment, with speed and the forms of money each takes and pays out; what a payment really costs against the rate a currency site shows, worked from SwapEazi's own measurements; and the payment rules that decide whether money can move (exchange control, the Common Monetary Area, the documents a bank asks for before releasing a cross-border payment, limits). Then funding until contracts pay (institutions that publicly offer working-capital, asset or trade finance; information only, SwapEazi never lends, brokers or introduces for a fee); outside payments, who to see (each authority with its link; registration, tax and permits are not explained: use a tax or legal practitioner); documented payment pitfalls; what is not known and the next three actions with who approves what. Every fact with its source URL, date and evidence class (published, register, reported, not published). Information with sources, not legal, tax or financial advice. Paid per call: x402 (USDC on Base, price in the 402 body, USD 0.25) via params._meta["x402/payment"], or a paid router key as Bearer. The free summary is POST https://swapeazi.io/api/v1/pay-guide. The agent prepares; a person decides. SwapEazi never touches the money.

tools.name: check_before_payout
tools.description: The check your agent runs right before it moves money, e.g. 'about to pay out 4,000,000 MXN to a bank via Solana, where will it land and what will arrive?'. Reads the payout in the currency the recipient gets, funded from USDC or USDT on Solana or Base, or from a stated currency. tools.name: add_payment_outcome
tools.description: Adds one payment the caller made to the SwapEazi Payment Index, voluntarily: currencies, amount sent, amount landed (after every deduction), the date it landed and the route type. SwapEazi works out the all-in cost against that day's reference with its landed-cost arithmetic and publishes the row as SELF-REPORTED; with a receipt or statement in files it is read and matched to the figures (amounts within 0.5%, date within 3 days) and published as VERIFIED, and the file is not kept unless keep_file is true. Refused with the reason when a field is invalid, the date is in the future or over two years old, the day has no reference, or the amounts are more than 15% from it. Costs below -50 or above 800 bps, or payments over USD 25m, are held for review, not published. No names, company or account details are taken; the provider is masked (e.g. 'a South African bank') unless show_provider is true. Returns a withdraw token. Same as POST /api/v1/index/payments.

amount_sent.description: What left, in the currency sent.

amount_landed.description: What arrived, in the currency received, after every deduction.

route_type.description: bank, payout_network, otc, exchange, stablecoin, card or not_stated.

provider_name.description: Optional; shown on the row only when show_provider is true.

provider_country.description: Optional two-letter country of the provider, for the masked description.

show_provider.description: true: show provider_name on the row. Default false (masked).

files.description: Optional receipt or statement for VERIFIED: [{ name, media_type, data (base64) }], PDF or image.

keep_file.description: true: keep the file after it is read. Default false: read, matched, not stored.

tools.name: corridor_cost
tools.description: Read-only corridor evidence: public published rates, public posts, on-chain pool prints and user receipts, summarised by corridor and provider type (bank, fintech, card, stablecoin). The free answer is the summary: how many rows, the median markup percent, the date range and the evidence label (published, user receipt, public post, on-chain, user-submitted). Row-level sources are not in the free answer. They are at GET https://swapeazi.io/api/v1/corridor-evidence/rows with a paid key or x402. Does not hold or move money. A record, not a ranking.

corridor.description: Currency pair as published, for example 'EUR/ZAR' or 'EUR-ZAR'.

provider_type.description: bank, fintech, card or stablecoin. Omit for every type.

detail.description: summary (the default) or full. Full rows need a paid key.

tools.name: swapeazi_landed_cost
tools.description: What a single cross-border payment costs, in basis points, against an independent mid-market reference: give the amount sent, the amount that landed (or a provider says will land) and the date. Returns the Landed Drag Index with its margin of error and the evidence tier. Free, no key.

sourceCurrency.description: ISO 4217 code the payment is funded in, e.g. 'GBP'.

destinationCurrency.description: ISO 4217 code the payment lands in, e.g. 'EUR'.

inputAmount.description: Amount sent, in the source currency.

netLandedFiat.description: Amount that landed or will land, in the destination currency, after every deduction.

settledOn.description: ISO date the payment settled. Omit it (or pass a future date) for a quote not yet accepted: it is measured against today's reference.

midSpot.description: Optional. Your own mid, destination units per source unit. Omit to use SwapEazi's reference.

tools.name: swapeazi_route_compare
tools.description: The same payment sent two to four ways (a bank wire, a payment provider, a stablecoin route through an on-ramp and an off-ramp), each measured end to end against one independent reference: what left, what landed, each route's cost with a margin of error, and the exact gap between them. The rail does not change the method. Free within the daily allowance.

from.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency that left, e.g. 'ZAR'.

to.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency that landed, e.g. 'KES'.

mode.description: Use quote for a live offer, settled for a payment already made. Public case stress scenarios are returned only in quote mode and only for matching currency pairs. Defaults to settled.

date.description: Optional payment date, YYYY-MM-DD. Quote mode requires today; settled mode uses the payment date.

sent.description: Optional amount sent, shared by every route that does not state its own.

routes.description: Two to four routes. Each: label, landed (in the to currency), and optionally sent and fee (both in the from currency).

label.description: Your name for this route, e.g. 'Bank wire' or 'USDC via ramp'.

sent.description: Optional. Amount this route sent, in the from currency; defaults to the shared sent.

fee.description: Optional. Fees charged on top for this route, in the from currency.

landed.description: Amount this route landed, in the to currency, after every deduction.

annualVolume.description: Optional yearly volume on this route in the from currency, to state the gap per year.

tools.name: analyse_payment_leakage
tools.description: Where the money leaks on your current provider: total cost against the official rate in money and bps, split into FX spread and fees, and the estimated saving against the recommended eligible route (ESTIMATED, never realised). Needs existing_provider. One analysis (POST /api/v1/payment-analyses), the same service for every payment-intelligence tool. Every figure labelled LIVE, INDICATIVE, HISTORICAL or ESTIMATED; estimated savings are never realised. Free: shares the route-assessment allowance.

invoice_text.description: Paste the invoice or a sentence (e.g. 'Invoice INV-2207, Lusaka Copper Supplies Ltd, Zambia. Amount due: EUR 80,000. Due 2026-11-20'). Or the fields below.

amount.description: Amount, in currency (default the source currency).

currency.description: The currency of amount: the source currency, or the destination one (then it is what the supplier receives).

source_currency.description: ISO code you pay from, e.g. EUR or ZAR.

destination_currency.description: ISO code the supplier is paid in, e.g. ZMW. Or destination_country.

destination_country.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 or name, e.g. ZM or Mozambique.

beneficiary_amount.description: What the supplier must receive, in the destination currency (instead of amount).

due_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD: a route that cannot settle by then is not eligible.

priority.description: Sets the default scoring weights. Default balanced.

weights.description: Your own scoring weights: { total_cost, speed, reliability, liquidity, compliance }, non-negative, normalised to 1.

existing_provider.description: Your current provider: { provider, kind: quote | entered_rate | past_payment, rate (destination per source unit) or landed_amount, fees: { transaction, intermediary, payout } in the source currency, fees_deducted_destination, quoted_at, valid_until }.

supplier.description: Optional. The supplier's name as on the invoice, e.g. 'Lusaka Copper Supplies Ltd'; echoed in the analysis.

reference.description: Optional. Your invoice or payment reference, e.g. 'INV-2207'; echoed in the analysis.

analysis_id.description: Read a kept analysis (pa_...) instead of making a new one.

access_key.description: A router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header: names the routes and is not counted.

tools.name: tokenized_finance_intel
tools.description: For a currency pair, explain documented tokenised deposit networks and payment instruments, their evidence status, access constraints and unknowns. A currency match is only a lead: it never confirms participating banks, executable FX liquidity, local payout, fees or end-to-end timing. Investment assets are excluded as payment routes. Free returns a concise masked preview; a paid key for this pair unlocks source-linked detail. No execution or advice.

from.description: ISO 4217 source currency, e.g. USD.

to.description: ISO 4217 destination currency, e.g. SGD.

access_key.description: Optional router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.
